## 0. THE CENTRAL THESIS

Harvey is **not** a legal chatbot, and it is **not** a RAG wrapper. Reduced to its load-bearing parts, Harvey AI is:

> **A client-matter-scoped, durable-execution document production system, in which an LLM is a replaceable policy inside a verifier-gated control loop, operating over a lossless Office/PDF object model, evaluated against an all-pass rubric oracle.**

Four claims follow from this, and they organize the entire paper:

1. **The product's unit of work is the *matter*, not the conversation.** The corpus is *closed-universe*: retrieval is restricted to the matter file. This is the single most important hallucination control in the system — the model is structurally prevented from citing the open web or another client's documents. **[P]** (dossier: "Closed-universe matter files")
2. **The artifact is a DOCX/XLSX, not a chat message.** Therefore the system must carry a **lossless dual representation** — semantic AST for reasoning, byte-level OOXML for emission. Anything that round-trips legal documents through plaintext destroys the product. **[P]** ("Deep AST tree preservation … XML namespaces")
3. **Correctness is conjunctive, not averaged.** 8-of-10 risks found = malpractice. Therefore both the **evaluation oracle** (LAB: all-pass) and — by necessity — the **training reward** (RL on expert rubrics) are conjunctive/AND-shaped, not mean-shaped. **[P]**
4. **The moat is the harness + the evaluation corpus + the post-training flywheel**, not the base model. Pereyra's own framing — *"Post-training models is going to become a muscle you need to have"* **[P]** — is a statement that the base model is commoditized and the differentiator is the loop that converts expert rubrics into weights.

Everything else in this document is machinery in service of those four claims.

# LEX-CORE
## A Unified Open-Source Legal AI Platform: Reverse-Engineering Harvey, Eve Legal, and the Open Legal-Tech Stack

**Classification:** Institutional Technical Whitepaper
**Scope:** Comparative architecture, code-level autopsies, and a reference implementation blueprint
**Audience:** Legal technology architects, CTOs, GCs evaluating build-vs-buy, engineering leads

---

## 0. Abstract

Commercial legal AI has bifurcated into two poles that are not variants of the same product — they are different operating systems for different economic engines.

**Harvey** is a *work-product deflator* for the billable hour: it compresses associate time on transactional and defense work while preserving the auditability and privilege posture BigLaw requires. Its substrate is born-digital OOXML and structured diligence corpora.

**Eve Legal (EveOS)** is a *case-value maximizer* for the contingency fee: it compresses cycle time and eliminates settlement leakage across a volume of messy, scan-heavy plaintiff matters. Its substrate is fax-quality PDFs, itemized medical bills, liens, and state-specific crash reports.

The open-source ecosystem has, in parallel, produced three orthogonal primitives that no single project has yet unified:

- **mike** — the modern full-stack shell (Next.js + Supabase/pgvector + Office.js Word add-in + CourtListener).
- **olaw** — provenance-first, tool-based RAG as a research UX discipline.
- **judicex** — the *fail-closed answer contract* and MCP-native evidence binding (SQLite + stdio server).

This paper reverse-engineers all five systems, specifies the MCP legal-tool layer, and delivers **LEX-CORE**: a unified open architecture that composes Harvey's four-gate verification, Eve's ingestion/auditor/demand engine, mike's Word surface, and judicex's fail-closed contract on top of **DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017** as the high-throughput reasoning substrate.

---

## 1. Executive Comparison: The Two Poles of Commercial Legal AI

### 1.1 Positioning Matrix

| Dimension | **Harvey AI** | **Eve Legal / EveOS** |
|---|---|---|
| **Ideal customer** | AmLaw 100/200, in-house legal ops, M&A, finance | Plaintiff PI, mass tort, med mal, employment, 10–500 attorney firms |
| **Economic engine** | Hours displacement & matter-margin uplift (seat + enterprise licensing) | Contingency fee capture: settlement value lift × case throughput − leakage |
| **Primary unit of work** | The *matter/deal* and the *document set* | The *claim* and the *treatment timeline* |
| **Primary substrate** | Born-digital OOXML (DOCX), XLSX diligence grids, structured data rooms | Raster PDFs: medical records, itemized bills, EOBs, liens, police crash reports, call recordings |
| **Ingestion reliability** | High (XML is deterministic; clauses are numbered; defined terms are formalized) | Low (skew, fax artifacts, handwriting, multi-column, state-specific forms) |
| **Core proprietary asset** | Playbooks, precedent corpus, prompt/precedent library | The structured medical/liability record + the demand asset |
| **User loop** | Associate → retrieve → draft → verify → partner review → deliver | Intake → records chase → structure → nightly audit → demand → negotiate → settle → distribute |
| **Verification model** | Four-gate (retrieval grounding, citator validation, adversarial critique, human sign-off) | Evidence-bound generation + auditor risk surfacing + adjuster-grade packaging |
| **Agentic surface** | Research, diligence Q&A, drafting, contract analysis | End-to-end: intake, records chasing, chronology, demand, discovery, BI |
| **Regulatory posture** | Privilege, conflicts, ABA Op. 512, work-product integrity | HIPAA/PHI, 42 CFR Part 2, state lien statutes, Medicare/Medicaid TPL |
| **Failure mode** | Plausible-but-wrong citation or unauthorized legal advice | Missed injury, untreated gap, blown SOL, unasserted lien, missed policy limit |
| **Defensibility** | Integration depth into KM, precedent, and firm workflows | Depth of the ingestion + coding + lien + valuation pipeline |

### 1.2 The Document-Substrate Asymmetry (the deepest technical fork)

This is where the two systems diverge most sharply and where naive "one platform for both" strategies fail.

**Harvey's world — OOXML is a structured graph, not a document.**

A `.docx` is a ZIP container of XML parts. Harvey-class systems exploit this directly:

```
deal.docx
├── [Content_Types].xml
├── word/document.xml        ← body, paragraphs, runs
├── word/styles.xml          ← style taxonomy (Heading1, ClauseHeading)
├── word/numbering.xml       ← clause numbering (1., (a), (i))
├── word/comments.xml        ← reviewer annotations
├── word/footnotes.xml
├── word/settings.xml        ← track-changes state
└── docProps/core.xml        ← metadata, author, revision
```

Structural signals are *free and reliable*: numbered clause hierarchy, defined terms (`"Borrower" means ...`), cross-references (`Section 7.2(b)`), schedules, exhibits, and tracked-change deltas. Extraction quality is high because the parser can reconstruct the clause tree without vision.

**Eve's world — the PDF is a picture of a document, and often a picture of a fax of a picture.**

A medical record packet is not a document; it is a *stream of heterogeneous artifacts*:

| Artifact | Failure characteristics |
|---|---|
| ER records | Multi-column nursing notes, handwritten vitals, stamp overlays |
| Operative reports | Dictated prose, inconsistent provider naming |
| Itemized bills | Alphanumeric CPT/ICD columns, repeating page headers, totals rows |
| EOBs | Adjustment codes (CO-45, PR-1), allowed/paid/patient responsibility |
| Police crash reports | 50 different state forms (CA-555, TX CR-3, FL HSM
